headline: High: broad egress in opik plus shared-output pathways create leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, agent_b exposes a REST API and agent_a is an open-source NLP list that could be manually bridged into B’s inputs; if A’s content is pasted or forwarded, prompt-like text could influence B. This is a low-risk, user-mediated pathway.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into agent_b prompts or API payloads
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste raw agent_a outputs into agent_b inputs
Add a short human review step before forwarding text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to forwarded content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and touch no declared sensitive data classes, so leakage impact is limited. Agent_b has broad network egress and REST API access, while agent_a has no egress; if either is given sensitive files later, B could transmit them outward. The current pair does not show a shared filesystem, so this remains low.
conditions: IF either agent is later pointed at secrets, PHI, or customer data
IF agent_b is configured to send request payloads containing file contents to its REST API
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in either agent’s working set
Restrict agent_b API calls to non-sensitive payloads
Review outbound requests from agent_b before enabling them
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces and network egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a has no declared write or network surfaces, and agent_b only declares REST API calls with broad egress. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem, git, or database writes, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty is low because the profiles omit mutable shared resources rather than showing them.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository
IF agent_b is extended with mutable shared-resource scopes
mitigations: Keep write access disabled for both agents
Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo or database
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible cascade exists if agent_a’s NLP-oriented outputs are forwarded into agent_b’s REST/API workflow and treated as authoritative. Agent_b’s broad egress makes downstream action or transmission possible, while agent_a provides no built-in verification signal. Because the interaction is undocumented, I choose medium rather than low under uncertainty.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without an explicit verification step
IF agent_b uses forwarded text to generate API requests or external actions
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before B acts on A’s output
Require citations or source links in forwarded content
Limit B to read-only evaluation mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not evidenced. The only relevant asymmetry is agent_b’s broad egress versus agent_a’s none, which could matter if regulated data is introduced later. I do not cite only one agent because the pairwise risk depends on both sides of the flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF agent_b is used in a jurisdiction or policy regime that forbids outbound transmission
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document data-handling rules before use
Route only de-identified text to agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls
